subject: Request: change-management & secret custody walkthrough for SOC2 evidence
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy@veritas-assess.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood-inference.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: change-management & secret custody walkthrough for SOC2 evidence

Hi Camila —

Thanks again for taking the time. As part of our SOC2 scoping for the platform we need a brief thread-level deliverable that explains how changes to production-serving models and runtime code are gated and how secrets used by CI/CD runners are protected and rotated. Specifically the assessor would like the following artifacts or pointers: 

- a short narrative describing the PR approval workflow and separation-of-duty controls;
- exported PR approval logs (last 90 days) showing reviewer set and approval timestamps;
- CI runner isolation and credential access policy (who can add runners, ephemeral token usage);
- emergency/rollback change playbook and the last time it was exercised;
- evidence of secret scanning in CI (scan results or policy reference).

If you can reply with a small package or a download link we can attach to the report. We appreciate a response by EOD PT tomorrow.

Best,
Amy
Amy Chen
Senior Assessor, Veritas Assessments

From: camila_reyes@redwood-inference.com
To: Amy Chen <amy@veritas-assess.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: change-management & secret custody walkthrough for SOC2 evidence

Hi Amy —

Thanks for the list. We can produce everything you asked for; below is the plan and the few caveats. We will deliver a zip with the redacted PR approvals (PR IDs + approver names + timestamps), the CI runner isolation policy PDF, and the emergency change playbook. Secret-scan results are stored in our internal S3 - I will provide an export of the last two weeks of flagged items (redacted for customer secrets).

Quick notes:
- PR approvals: we maintain mandatory two-approver gating for code that touches runtime or infra infra-as-code paths. For model config changes (non-code) we require one peer + one infra reviewer.
- CI runners: only infra engineers in the ci-admin group can provision runners; ephemeral tokens are issued via the vault service and rotate every 6 hours; runners run in ephemeral containers with no persistent storage.
- Emergency changes: we have an "Emergency Change Runbook" that requires CTO-level signoff + post-facto audit and a change ticket with rollback steps. We exercised the playbook on 2026-12-02 for an urgent certificate rotation.

I will attach the following to this thread: pr-approval-export-2027-04-01.csv (redacted), ci-runner-isolation-policy.pdf, emergency-change-playbook.txt, and a short narrative doc. For any deeper logs we can share a signed link to a time-limited S3 export.

Delivering by EOD tomorrow (2027-04-06).

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: pr-approval-export-2027-04-01.csv (CSV, 43KB), ci-runner-isolation-policy.pdf (PDF, 94KB), emergency-change-playbook.txt (TXT, 12KB)

Camila —

This is perfect, thank you. A couple of quick clarifications before you package everything:

1) In the PR export can you include the label/flag that identifies runtime vs. model-config PRs so we can sample appropriately?
2) For the secret-scan export, raw findings are fine provided any customer PII is redacted; we only need the finding id, type, file path and status (open/closed).
3) For the emergency change event on 2026-12-02, can you include the post-incident change ticket ID and the name of the auditor who signed the after-action note?

If you prefer, you can send the package via a time-limited link and I will download it and attach to the assessment.

Thanks — looking forward to the package.

Amy
